A FlowBoundary adds water to the model at a specified flow rate.
It can be used as a boundary condition like a measured upstream flow rate, or lateral inflow.
We require that a link connected to a FlowBoundary is always outgoing, and points towards a Basin.

# Allowed connectivity

The diagram below shows which node types are allowed directly upstream (left) and downstream (right) of this node.
This is a connectivity illustration, not a valid simulation model.

```{julia}
# | code-fold: true
include("../../../utils/plot_node_connectivity.jl")
plot_node_connectivity("FlowBoundary")
```

# Tables

## Static

```{julia}
# | code-fold: true
include("../../../utils/gen_docs_table.jl")
table_from_schema(
    Ribasim.Schema.FlowBoundary.Static;
    restrictions = Dict(:flow_rate => "non-negative"),
)
```

## Time

This table is the transient form of the `FlowBoundary` table.
The difference is that a time column is added, and an optional interpolation column.
With this the flow rates can be updated over time. In between the given times the
flow rate is interpolated, and outside the flow rate is constant given by the
nearest time value unless the node is cyclic in time.
Note that a `node_id` can be either in this table or in the static one, but not both.

The `interpolation` column sets the interpolation type per node, either `block` or `linear`.
It cannot change over time, so it must have the same value in all rows of a node.
If it is missing, the `flow_boundary` interpolation type from the [interpolation settings](/reference/usage.qmd#interpolation-settings) is used, which is `block` by default.

```{julia}
# | code-fold: true
table_from_schema(
    Ribasim.Schema.FlowBoundary.Time;
    restrictions = Dict(
        :flow_rate => "non-negative",
        :interpolation => "block or linear, constant per node",
    ),
)
```

## Concentration {#sec-flow-boundary-conc}
This table defines the concentration of substances for the flow from the FlowBoundary.

```{julia}
# | code-fold: true
table_from_schema(
    Ribasim.Schema.FlowBoundary.Concentration;
    restrictions = Dict(:substance => "can correspond to known Delwaq substances"),
)
```

## Area

The optional area table is not used during computation, but provides a place to associate areas in the form of polygons to a FlowBoundary.
Using this makes it easier to recognize which water or land surfaces are represented by a FlowBoundary.

column    | type                    | restriction
--------- | ----------------------- | -----------
node_id   | Int32                   |
geom      | Polygon or MultiPolygon | (optional)

# Equations

A FlowBoundary can be connected directly to a Basin and prescribes the flow to that Basin.
Since the `flow_rate` cannot be negative a FlowBoundary can only add water to the model.

# Behavior in allocation

Allocation cannot change the flow of a FlowBoundary.
Each time [allocation](/concept/allocation.qmd) runs, it assumes the flow of the FlowBoundary stays at its current value until the next intervention time, set by `intervention_interval` in the [allocation settings](/reference/usage.qmd#sec-allocation-settings), so it does not anticipate later changes in the timeseries.
When the flow changes in between, the water that is actually available differs from what allocation planned with.
The flow of a FlowBoundary can be used to supply demands downstream.
